seo.meta_description: GlobalMed provides enterprise telehealth hardware (carts, stations) and software (eNcounter) for hospitals and DoD. SOC 2 certified. ISO 13485 manufacturer.

faqs.a: Enterprise telehealth company that sells both hardware (telemedicine carts, wall-mounted stations, ruggedized mobile cases) and software (eNcounter platform). They serve hospitals, health systems, and military/DoD. Not a fit for small practices—this is enterprise infrastructure.

Telemedicine carts with integrated medical devices (stethoscopes, otoscopes, cameras), wall-mounted stations, and ruggedized backpack/hard-case units for field deployment. ISO 13485 certified manufacturer supporting 60+ virtual care modalities.

Their software platform that goes beyond basic video calls. Features AI-powered triage (assesses symptoms, routes to specialists, pre-populates notes), EHR integration, multi-modal care support, and customizable workflows.

faqs.q: Is GlobalMed approved for government/military use?
faqs.a: Yes. GlobalMed holds Defense Health Agency Authority to Operate (ATO) for DoD networks—renewed December 2025. This is the highest security benchmark for telehealth vendors, validating hardware, software, and operational procedures together.

faqs.q: What security certifications does GlobalMed have?
faqs.a: HIPAA compliant, SOC 2 Type II certified, DoD ATO, and Microsoft Gold Partner. Their integrated hardware/software approach allows for more comprehensive security validation than software-only platforms.

faqs.q: How does GlobalMed compare to Teladoc or Amwell?
faqs.a: Different category. Teladoc and Amwell are consumer-facing telehealth services. GlobalMed sells the infrastructure (hardware + software) that health systems use to build their own telehealth programs. GlobalMed competes with Avizia (Amwell enterprise), InTouch Health, and similar enterprise vendors.
